description: Hi! I'm a second-year nursing student interested in space medicine. My idea is an AI-powered system that uses astronauts' gathered health data to personalize daily schedules, adjusting exercise, hydration, recovery, and sleep while supporting crew autonomy.
summary: We developed a spaceflight gamification and health simulation engine to safeguard astronaut health on long duration space missions. It addresses the core hazards of spaceflight by evaluating real time telemetry against clinical thresholds and triggering targeted countermeasure quests, ranging from exercise protocols to radiation emergency drills. This system is vital for preventing severe physiological degradation during Artemis and Mars journeys.
details:
As the creators of the Spaceflight Gamification & Health Simulation Engine, we developed a platform to model and mitigate deep-spaceflight hazards on missions to Low Earth Orbit, the Moon, and Mars. The engine systematically tackles the RIDGE framework—radiation, isolation, distance, gravity fields, and hostile environments—across five key anatomical systems: brain and eyes, cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, immune and gut, and cellular integrity.

The platform ingests real-time biometric and environmental telemetry, including optical coherence tomography scans, cardiovascular metrics, bone density logs, sleep actigraphy, and neutron flux from the Canadian Active Neutron Spectrometer. It evaluates these against clinical thresholds from NASA’s Human Research Program and the Canadian Space Agency, while connecting to NASA's DONKI API for live solar weather alerts.

To drive crew compliance, the engine transforms medical countermeasures into engaging, gamified quests and workflows. Routine tasks include high-load resistance training, cardio sprints, venous occlusion thigh-cuffs, and smart-lighting circadian schedules, alongside automated emergency protocols for solar particle storms. Ultimately, this project prevents severe physiological degradation like SANS and acute radiation syndrome, fusing aerospace medicine with interactive gaming loops to safeguard astronaut health and ensure crew survival during deep-space exploration.
